subtopic: Legal Frameworks, Code of Ethics, PPST, & Philosophies

items.term: Republic Act No. 7836 (Philippine Teachers Professionalization Act of 1994)
items.definition: The landmark Philippine law that officially recognized teaching as a regulated profession, creating the Board for Professional Teachers under the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) and mandating the Licensure Examination for Teachers (LET).
items.rationalization: Enacted on December 15, 1994; transferred the regulation and licensure of professional teachers from the Civil Service Commission and DECS to the PRC.

mnemonic.title: RA 7836 Law
mnemonic.phrase: 7836 = Professional Licensure for Teachers

items.tosCompetency: Analyze legal mandates governing the teaching profession in the Philippines

items.definition: The law amending RA 7836 that introduced special temporary permits for para-teachers and required non-practicing professional teachers who have not taught for five consecutive years to take a 12-unit refresher course.
items.rationalization: Signed in 2004 to address teaching shortages in remote areas and ensure that inactive licensed teachers update their pedagogical content knowledge before returning to the classroom.

mnemonic.title: RA 9293 Amendments
mnemonic.phrase: 9293 = Para-Teachers and 12-Unit Refresher
items: 12 units - Refresher course after 5 inactive years

items.tosCompetency: Analyze legal mandates governing the teaching profession in the Philippines

items.definition: The initial decree signed by President Ferdinand Marcos declaring teaching as a profession and instituting the first Civil Service-administered teacher examinations in the Philippines.
items.rationalization: Decree Professionalizing Teaching; established the National Board for Teachers (NBT); later superseded and modernized by Republic Act No. 7836.

mnemonic.title: PD 1006 Pioneer
mnemonic.phrase: PD 1006 = First Decree Professionalizing Teaching

items.tosCompetency: Analyze legal mandates governing the teaching profession in the Philippines

items.term: Republic Act No. 4670 (Magna Carta for Public School Teachers)
items.definition: The fundamental law promoting and improving the socio-economic status of public school teachers, their living and working conditions, employment terms, and career prospects.
items.rationalization: Enacted in June 1966; provides landmark protections including maximum 6 hours of actual classroom teaching, hardship allowance, paid study leaves, and security of tenure.

mnemonic.title: Magna Carta RA 4670
mnemonic.phrase: 4670 = Rights and Welfare of Public Teachers

items.tosCompetency: Analyze legal mandates governing the teaching profession in the Philippines

items.term: Six (6) Hours Maximum Classroom Teaching (RA 4670 Section 13)
items.definition: The statutory limit mandating that any teacher engaged in actual classroom instruction shall not be required to render more than six hours of actual teaching a day.
items.rationalization: The remaining two hours of the eight-hour working day are allocated to lesson preparation, checking exercises, grading, and parent conferences; teaching in excess of 6 hours requires additional compensation of at least 25% of regular pay.

mnemonic.title: Six-Hour Rule
mnemonic.phrase: 6 Hours Teaching + 2 Hours Preparation = 8 Hours

items.tosCompetency: Analyze legal mandates governing the teaching profession in the Philippines

items.definition: A special additional financial compensation of at least 25% of monthly salary paid to public school teachers assigned to remote, hazardous, isolated, or difficult hardship posts.
items.rationalization: Compensates teachers who endure geographic hazards, lack of public transport, mountain treks, or insurgency risks in rural assignments.

mnemonic.title: Hardship Allowance
mnemonic.phrase: At Least 25% Extra for Difficult Stations

items.tosCompetency: Analyze legal mandates governing the teaching profession in the Philippines

items.term: Study Leave with Pay (Sabbatical / RA 4670 Section 24)
items.definition: The right of public school teachers who have rendered at least seven (7) years of continuous service to a study leave not exceeding one year with at least 60% of their regular monthly salary.
items.rationalization: Granted to pursue graduate studies or academic specialization; requires a return service agreement of two years for every year of paid study leave.

mnemonic.title: Study Leave Rule
mnemonic.phrase: 7 Years Service = 1 Year Leave with 60% Pay

items.tosCompetency: Analyze legal mandates governing the teaching profession in the Philippines

items.term: Republic Act No. 10533 (Enhanced Basic Education Act of 2013)
items.definition: The law expanding the Philippine basic education cycle from 10 to 13 years, creating the K to 12 basic education program (Kindergarten, 6 years Elementary, 4 years JHS, 2 years SHS).
items.rationalization: Mandated Mother Tongue-Based Multilingual Education (MTB-MLE) from Kindergarten to Grade 3, a spiral progression curriculum, and specialized Senior High School academic/technical tracks.

mnemonic.title: RA 10533 K-12
mnemonic.phrase: 10533 = K to 12 Enhanced Basic Education

items.tosCompetency: Analyze legal mandates governing the teaching profession in the Philippines

items.definition: The foundational statement establishing that professional teachers are duly licensed professionals who possess dignity and reputation with high moral values, technical and professional competence.
items.rationalization: Sets the high standard that teaching is not merely a job, but a noble public trust requiring continuous ethical dedication and adherence to professional standards.

mnemonic.title: Ethics Preamble
mnemonic.phrase: Dignity, Moral Values, and Professional Competence

items.tosCompetency: Apply the Code of Ethics for Professional Teachers to ethical dilemmas

items.term: Code of Ethics: Article II - The Teacher and the State
items.definition: The ethical provisions outlining a teacher's civic responsibilities, including loyalty to the Constitution, obedience to laws, exercising the right to vote, and the strict prohibition against using one's position to proselytize or coerce partisan political votes.
items.rationalization: Section 5 affirms academic freedom while emphasizing that teachers must not engage in partisan political campaigns in the classroom or spread subversive propaganda.

mnemonic.title: Article II State
mnemonic.phrase: Loyal Citizen, Neutral in Partisan Politics

items.tosCompetency: Apply the Code of Ethics for Professional Teachers to ethical dilemmas

items.term: Code of Ethics: Article III - The Teacher and the Community
items.definition: The ethical mandate that teachers must render leadership in community initiatives, refrain from gambling and drunkenness, and study local customs to foster mutual respect.
items.rationalization: Section 1 declares that the teacher is a facilitator of learning and development in the community; expected to provide intellectual leadership in barangay projects without partisan bias.

mnemonic.title: Article III Community
mnemonic.phrase: Community Leader, Respect Local Traditions

items.tosCompetency: Apply the Code of Ethics for Professional Teachers to ethical dilemmas

items.term: Code of Ethics: Article VIII - The Teacher and the Learners
items.definition: The ethical provisions governing teacher-student relationships, mandating fairness in grading, zero corporal punishment, and strict professional protocol regarding romantic relationships.
items.rationalization: Section 7 dictates: In a situation where mutual attraction and subsequent love develop between teacher and student, the teacher shall exercise utmost professional discretion to avoid favoritism, and transfer the student to another teacher if necessary.

mnemonic.title: Article VIII Learners
mnemonic.phrase: No Corporal Punishment, Pure Professional Discretion

items.tosCompetency: Apply the Code of Ethics for Professional Teachers to ethical dilemmas

items.term: Prohibition of Corporal Punishment (Article VIII Section 8)
items.definition: The strict ethical and legal mandate that no teacher shall inflict corporal punishment on offending learners nor make deductions from their scholastic ratings as a penalty for acts which are clearly not manifestations of poor scholarship.
items.rationalization: Reinforced by the Child Protection Policy (DepEd Order No. 40 s. 2012); corporal punishment (slapping, pinching, kneeling on salt, verbal humiliation) constitutes administrative misconduct and child abuse.

mnemonic.title: No Corporal Punishment
mnemonic.phrase: Zero Physical or Humiliating Discipline

items.tosCompetency: Apply the Code of Ethics for Professional Teachers to ethical dilemmas

items.term: Code of Ethics: Article X - The Teacher and Business
items.definition: The ethical rule prohibiting teachers from using their authority to coerce students or parents to purchase personal commercial products, merchandise, or study materials.
items.rationalization: Section 1 upholds that a teacher has the right to engage in legitimate business, provided it does not adversely affect professional performance; Section 2 forbids selling items directly to one's own students.

mnemonic.title: Article X Business
mnemonic.phrase: No Peddling Merchandise to Your Students
items: No selling goods to own pupils

items.tosCompetency: Apply the Code of Ethics for Professional Teachers to ethical dilemmas

items.term: Philippine Professional Standards for Teachers (PPST / DO 42 s. 2017)
items.definition: The national framework establishing clear expectations of teacher quality across seven domains, 37 strands, and four developmental career stages.
items.rationalization: Replaced the National Competency-Based Teacher Standards (NCBTS); aligns teacher performance with the K to 12 reform and the ASEAN Qualifications Reference Framework.

mnemonic.title: PPST Framework
mnemonic.phrase: 7 Domains, 37 Strands, 4 Career Stages

items.tosCompetency: Differentiate the 7 Domains and 4 Career Stages of the PPST

items.definition: The entry career stage representing newly qualified licensed teachers who possess the required qualifications, strong content knowledge, and enthusiasm, seeking guidance from mentor teachers.
items.rationalization: Beginning teachers need coaching in managing classroom behavior, addressing student diversity, and preparing valid assessment tools during their initial years.

mnemonic.title: PPST Stage 1
mnemonic.phrase: Beginning = Newly Licensed, Needs Mentorship

items.tosCompetency: Differentiate the 7 Domains and 4 Career Stages of the PPST

items.definition: The career stage representing professionally independent practitioners who display pedagogical skill, effectively manage learning environments, and independently facilitate learner achievement.
items.rationalization: They design engaging lesson plans, administer varied formative and summative assessments, and collaborate with colleagues to improve school outcomes.

mnemonic.title: PPST Stage 2
mnemonic.phrase: Proficient = Professionally Independent Practitioner

items.tosCompetency: Differentiate the 7 Domains and 4 Career Stages of the PPST

items.term: PPST Career Stage 3: Highly Proficient Teachers
items.definition: The career stage representing experienced master teachers who consistently display high levels of classroom excellence, mentor colleagues, and lead instructional innovations in their department.
items.rationalization: Master Teachers in this stage serve as demonstration teachers, action researchers, and mentors to Beginning and Proficient colleagues.

mnemonic.title: PPST Stage 3
mnemonic.phrase: Highly Proficient = Master Teacher and Mentor

items.tosCompetency: Differentiate the 7 Domains and 4 Career Stages of the PPST

items.definition: The pinnacle career stage representing educational leaders recognized at the division, regional, and national levels who spearhead major curriculum policies and inspire the entire profession.
items.rationalization: They embody the highest standard of teaching practice, formulate pedagogical research, and advise educational policymakers on national curriculum improvements.

mnemonic.title: PPST Stage 4
mnemonic.phrase: Distinguished = Pinnacle Leader and Innovator

items.tosCompetency: Differentiate the 7 Domains and 4 Career Stages of the PPST

items.term: PPST Domain 1: Content Knowledge and Pedagogy
items.definition: The PPST domain requiring teachers to demonstrate deep mastery of subject matter, integrate interdisciplinary connections, use mother tongue, and apply research-based pedagogical principles.
items.rationalization: Ensures teachers do not simply teach superficial facts, but facilitate critical thinking, problem-solving, and literacy across curriculum areas.

mnemonic.title: PPST Domain 1
mnemonic.phrase: Domain 1 = Subject Mastery and Teaching Skills

items.tosCompetency: Differentiate the 7 Domains and 4 Career Stages of the PPST

items.definition: The PPST domain focused on establishing safe, secure, fair, and supportive physical and psychological classroom environments that promote purposeful learning.
items.rationalization: Encompasses classroom management, positive discipline, motivating learner engagement, and fostering a collaborative, bully-free atmosphere.

mnemonic.title: PPST Domain 2
mnemonic.phrase: Domain 2 = Safe, Secure, Positive Classroom

items.tosCompetency: Differentiate the 7 Domains and 4 Career Stages of the PPST

items.definition: The PPST domain emphasizing responsive teaching that accommodates learners' gender, needs, strengths, interests, socioeconomic status, disabilities, giftedness, and indigenous backgrounds.
items.rationalization: Requires differentiated instruction and culturally sensitive pedagogies that ensure every child thrives regardless of exceptionality or background.

mnemonic.title: PPST Domain 3
mnemonic.phrase: Domain 3 = Inclusive of All Diverse Learners

items.tosCompetency: Differentiate the 7 Domains and 4 Career Stages of the PPST

items.definition: The PPST domain addressing how teachers align lesson objectives with national curriculum standards (DepEd K to 12), sequence learning experiences, and select effective instructional materials.
items.rationalization: Covers daily lesson planning (DLP/DLL), contextualizing lessons to local community reality, and ensuring seamless spiral progression.

mnemonic.title: PPST Domain 4
mnemonic.phrase: Domain 4 = Lesson Planning and Curriculum Alignment

items.tosCompetency: Differentiate the 7 Domains and 4 Career Stages of the PPST

items.definition: The PPST domain mandating the design and use of diagnostic, formative, and summative assessments, data analysis, and transparent reporting of student progress to parents.
items.rationalization: Ensures assessments are valid, reliable, and aligned with learning competencies; uses assessment data to provide constructive feedback and reteach unmastered concepts.

mnemonic.title: PPST Domain 5
mnemonic.phrase: Domain 5 = Testing, Grading, and Parent Reporting

items.tosCompetency: Differentiate the 7 Domains and 4 Career Stages of the PPST

items.term: PPST Domain 6: Community Linkages and Professional Engagement
items.definition: The PPST domain involving constructive partnerships with parents, barangay officials, local industry, and alumni to enrich the school environment.
items.rationalization: Focuses on school-community synergy, organizing Brigada Eskwela, PTA assemblies, and upholding the Code of Ethics in community interactions.

mnemonic.title: PPST Domain 6
mnemonic.phrase: Domain 6 = School-Community Partnerships

items.tosCompetency: Differentiate the 7 Domains and 4 Career Stages of the PPST

items.term: PPST Domain 7: Personal Growth and Professional Development
items.definition: The PPST domain prioritizing a teacher's continuous professional growth, reflective practice, attendance in seminars/workshops, mental health, and professional philosophy.
items.rationalization: Recognizes that teacher quality requires lifelong learning; teachers continually evaluate their own practice to improve instructional impact.

mnemonic.title: PPST Domain 7
mnemonic.phrase: Domain 7 = Lifelong Learning and Reflection

items.tosCompetency: Differentiate the 7 Domains and 4 Career Stages of the PPST

items.definition: The philosophical doctrine founded by Plato holding that reality is fundamentally spiritual, mental, and conceptual, with immutable ideas being the ultimate truth.
items.rationalization: Curriculum emphasizes enduring ideas, literature, mathematics, and philosophy; teaching relies on the Socratic question-and-answer method to draw out latent knowledge.

mnemonic.title: Idealism Clue
mnemonic.phrase: Plato: Ideas in the Mind are Real

items.tosCompetency: Compare classical and contemporary philosophies of education

items.definition: The philosophy founded by Aristotle holding that reality exists independently of the human mind, and that truth is discovered through sensory observation and empirical science.
items.rationalization: Emphasizes the natural sciences, objective facts, sensory experiments, and direct demonstration; reality is what can be measured and observed.

mnemonic.title: Realism Clue
mnemonic.phrase: Aristotle: Physical World Proven by Senses

items.tosCompetency: Compare classical and contemporary philosophies of education

items.definition: The student-centered philosophy championed by John Dewey asserting that education is life itself, rooted in 'learning by doing', experiential problem-solving, and democratic inquiry.
items.rationalization: Rejects passive rote memorization; students engage in hands-on projects, group cooperation, and real-life scientific experiments adapting to a changing world.

mnemonic.title: Progressivism Clue
mnemonic.phrase: John Dewey: Learning by Doing

items.tosCompetency: Compare classical and contemporary philosophies of education

items.definition: The traditional, teacher-centered philosophy formulated by William Bagley holding that schools should focus on rigorous mastery of the basic skills (the 3Rs: Reading, wRiting, aRithmetic) and core academic subjects.
items.rationalization: The teacher is the sole authoritarian expert transmitting essential cultural heritage and academic discipline; emphasizes hard work and factual mastery.

mnemonic.title: Essentialism Clue
mnemonic.phrase: Back to the Basics: 3 Rs and Core Subjects

items.tosCompetency: Compare classical and contemporary philosophies of education

items.definition: The conservative educational philosophy spearheaded by Robert Hutchins and Mortimer Adler asserting that truth is universal and unchanging, and education should focus on timeless enduring ideas found in the 'Great Books'.
items.rationalization: Believes human nature remains constant across centuries; students study Shakespeare, Aristotle, and Newton to cultivate timeless rational intellect.

mnemonic.title: Perennialism Clue
mnemonic.phrase: Perennial = Everlasting Truths & Great Books

items.tosCompetency: Compare classical and contemporary philosophies of education

items.definition: The individualistic philosophy influenced by Jean-Paul Sartre and Soren Kierkegaard asserting that existence precedes essence, and education should empower learners to freely define their own identity and personal values.
items.rationalization: Curriculum offers wide elective choices; students take complete personal responsibility for their choices, rejecting conformity and external dogmatic mandates.

mnemonic.title: Existentialism Clue
mnemonic.phrase: Existence Precedes Essence: Freedom of Choice
items: F - Freedom to choose personal path

items.tosCompetency: Compare classical and contemporary philosophies of education

items.definition: The educational philosophy founded by John Watson and B.F. Skinner holding that human behavior is shaped entirely by environmental stimuli, conditioning, and reinforcement.
items.rationalization: Learning is defined as an observable change in behavior; teachers use positive reinforcement (rewards, praise) and negative reinforcement to condition student learning.

mnemonic.title: Behaviorism Clue
mnemonic.phrase: Skinner: Stimulus, Response, Reinforcement

items.tosCompetency: Compare classical and contemporary philosophies of education

items.definition: The transformative philosophy founded by Theodore Brameld and George Counts arguing that schools should be agents of social change, leading society to reconstruct and eliminate poverty, racism, and inequality.
items.rationalization: Challenges oppressive social structures; teachers encourage students to critically examine real-world social injustices and propose revolutionary solutions for a better world.

mnemonic.title: Reconstructionism Clue
mnemonic.phrase: Schools as Agents to Reconstruct Society

items.tosCompetency: Compare classical and contemporary philosophies of education

items.definition: The contemporary learning philosophy rooted in Piaget and Vygotsky asserting that learners actively construct their own subjective knowledge by connecting new information with existing cognitive schema.
items.rationalization: The teacher acts as a facilitator and guide on the side rather than an all-knowing dispenser of facts, encouraging discovery, inquiry, and peer collaboration.

mnemonic.title: Constructivism Clue
mnemonic.phrase: Learners Build Their Own Meaning

items.tosCompetency: Compare classical and contemporary philosophies of education

items.definition: The dimension of teaching characterized by long years of specialized tertiary preparation, a rigorous licensure examination, adherence to a Code of Ethics, and continuing professional development.
items.rationalization: Differentiates teaching from casual employment; licensed teachers are members of an accredited professional organization bound by high public standards.

mnemonic.title: Teaching Profession
mnemonic.phrase: Licensure, Specialized Preparation, Code of Ethics

items.tosCompetency: Synthesize teaching as a profession, vocation, and mission

items.definition: The perspective viewing teaching as an internal calling (from Latin 'vocare', to call) to dedicate one's life selflessly to educating and nurturing the young.
items.rationalization: Teaching is undertaken not solely for monetary compensation, but out of personal passion, profound love for children, and inner fulfillment.

mnemonic.title: Teaching Vocation
mnemonic.phrase: Vocare: A Sacred Calling from the Heart

items.tosCompetency: Synthesize teaching as a profession, vocation, and mission

items.definition: The perspective viewing teaching as an assigned task (from Latin 'mittere', to send) entrusted by society to make the world better by transforming student lives.
items.rationalization: A teacher is 'sent' to eradicate ignorance, inspire dreams, and build upright citizens; involves clear objectives, accountability, and unrelenting perseverance.

mnemonic.title: Teaching Mission
mnemonic.phrase: Mittere: Sent with a Sacred Task

items.tosCompetency: Synthesize teaching as a profession, vocation, and mission

items.definition: The comprehensive legislation establishing and maintaining an integrated system of education in the Philippines, delineating the rights and obligations of students, teachers, administrators, and parents.
items.rationalization: Guarantees teachers the right to free expression of opinions, freedom from compulsory non-academic deductions, and professional advancement opportunities.

mnemonic.title: BP 232 Framework
mnemonic.phrase: Education Act of 1982: Integrated Educational System

items.tosCompetency: Analyze legal mandates governing the teaching profession in the Philippines

items.term: DepEd Order No. 40 s. 2012: Child Protection Policy
items.definition: The landmark policy adopting zero tolerance for all forms of child abuse, exploitation, violence, discrimination, bullying, and corporal punishment in basic education institutions.
items.rationalization: Requires every public and private school to form a Child Protection Committee (CPC) to handle complaints and safeguard child rights in the classroom.

mnemonic.title: Child Protection Policy
mnemonic.phrase: Zero Tolerance for Child Abuse and Bullying

items.tosCompetency: Apply child protection policies and school child rights protocols

items.definition: The law requiring licensed professionals, including teachers, to earn CPD credit units through formal and non-formal trainings as a mandatory prerequisite for PRC professional license renewal.
items.rationalization: Ensures teachers continually update their competencies with evolving global educational standards throughout their career lifecycle.

mnemonic.title: CPD Act RA 10912
mnemonic.phrase: 10912 = CPD Credit Units for PRC License

items.tosCompetency: Analyze legal mandates governing the teaching profession in the Philippines

items.definition: The law institutionalizing kindergarten into the basic education system, making pre-school education mandatory and compulsory for all 5-year-old Filipino children before admission to Grade 1.
items.rationalization: Passed in 2011 to establish the foundational cognitive, physical, and socio-emotional readiness essential for academic success in elementary schooling.

mnemonic.title: RA 10157 Kindergarten
mnemonic.phrase: 10157 = Mandatory Kindergarten at Age 5

items.tosCompetency: Analyze legal mandates governing the teaching profession in the Philippines

items.term: Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act (RA 10931)
items.definition: The 2017 law providing tuition-free higher education to Filipino students enrolled in State Universities and Colleges (SUCs) and Local Universities and Colleges (LUCs).
items.rationalization: Democratized access to tertiary education, significantly benefiting pre-service teacher education students from low-income families.

mnemonic.title: RA 10931 Free Tuition
mnemonic.phrase: 10931 = Free College Tuition in SUCs

items.tosCompetency: Analyze legal mandates governing the teaching profession in the Philippines

items.term: Article XIV Section 5(5) of the 1987 Constitution: Education Budget Priority
items.definition: The constitutional mandate directing that the State shall assign the highest budgetary priority to education to ensure that teaching will attract and retain its rightful share of the best available talents.
items.rationalization: Ensures the Department of Education receives the largest budgetary allocation among all government executive departments in the national budget.

mnemonic.title: Highest Budget Mandate
mnemonic.phrase: Constitution: Highest Budget to Education
items: Attract the best talents to teaching

items.tosCompetency: Analyze legal mandates governing the teaching profession in the Philippines

items.term: Teacher's Academic Freedom in Higher Education
items.definition: The constitutional right guaranteed to faculty members in institutions of higher learning to investigate, teach, and publish research findings without administrative or political censorship.
items.rationalization: Recognized in Article XIV Section 5(2) of the 1987 Constitution; applies primarily to colleges and universities; basic education teachers follow the prescribed curriculum.

mnemonic.title: Academic Freedom
mnemonic.phrase: Higher Ed Faculty Freedom to Research and Teach

items.tosCompetency: Analyze legal mandates governing the teaching profession in the Philippines

items.term: DepEd Order No. 42 s. 2016: Lesson Preparation Policy
items.definition: The policy guidelines on daily lesson preparation, distinguishing between the Detailed Lesson Plan (DLP) required of newly hired teachers and the Daily Lesson Log (DLL) used by experienced teachers.
items.rationalization: Teachers with at least one year of teaching experience may use the DLL; teachers in their first year of service must prepare the DLP covering all instructional components.

mnemonic.title: DLP vs DLL Rules
mnemonic.phrase: DLP for First-Year Teachers; DLL for Experienced

items.tosCompetency: Apply DepEd policies on lesson planning and instructional delivery

items.term: Teachers' Dignified Living and Decorum (Code of Ethics Article XI)
items.definition: The ethical standard requiring that a teacher shall maintain a dignified personality, live a modest and moral life, and practice financial prudence to avoid scandalous debts.
items.rationalization: Section 3 mandates: A teacher shall maintain at all times a dignified personality which could serve as a model worthy of emulation by learners, peers, and others.

mnemonic.title: Article XI Decorum
mnemonic.phrase: Modest Life and Moral Role Model

items.tosCompetency: Apply the Code of Ethics for Professional Teachers to ethical dilemmas

items.definition: The collegial body under the administrative supervision of the PRC composed of five members appointed by the President of the Philippines to formulate, administer, and supervise the LET.
items.rationalization: Authorized to issue, suspend, or revoke professional teacher licenses for causes such as immoral conduct, gross incompetence, negligence, or malpractice.

mnemonic.title: BPT PRC Powers
mnemonic.phrase: 5 Members Who Administer and Regulate the LET

items.tosCompetency: Analyze legal mandates governing the teaching profession in the Philippines

items.definition: The statutory penalty stripping a teacher of their certificate of registration and license for conviction of a crime involving moral turpitude, immoral conduct, gross incompetence, or cheating on the board exam.
items.rationalization: A teacher whose license is revoked cannot practice teaching in any public or private school anywhere in the Philippines.

mnemonic.title: License Revocation
mnemonic.phrase: Lost License for Immorality or Cheating

items.tosCompetency: Analyze legal mandates governing the teaching profession in the Philippines

items.term: The Four Pillars of Education (UNESCO / Delors Report)
items.definition: The international vision of lifelong education: Learning to KNOW (mastery of learning tools), Learning to DO (skills & application), Learning to LIVE TOGETHER (empathy & peace), and Learning to BE (complete human development).
items.rationalization: Chaired by Jacques Delors in 1996; emphasizes that education must nurture holistic human potential rather than mere rote intellectual knowledge.

mnemonic.title: Four Delors Pillars
mnemonic.phrase: Know, Do, Live Together, Be

items.tosCompetency: Synthesize global frameworks (UNESCO 4 Pillars) in teacher education
